answer: In an agent marketplace trading velvet, shale, and sonnet commissions, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow, never to account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives exactly the same total voting weight as one agent holding 100. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the escrow period regardless of how many identities they invent.
